explanation: A second-member head: on ordinary prose it is silent (strength 0, attention parked on the first token), and it fires (0.5-1.3) only where the text builds a second member that matches an earlier one, attending ~1.0 to the earlier member's head word. Predicted active: (a) code, markup, SQL, JSON, config and templated rows (nearly every line after the first); (b) the 'to'/'and' of a 'from X to Y' or 'between X and Y' range whose endpoints are words, years or numbers with units; (c) the second copy of a repeated phrase of three or more tokens or of a multi-token name; (d) separators of lists of three or more items joined by commas, semicolons, '&', '||' or 'and' (about two in three such lists cross), and, more weakly (about half), the 'and'/'or' of a noun-phrase pair such as 'my aunt and my uncle'. Predicted inactive: single plain sentences and short multi-sentence prose with none of these (about one in fifteen crosses weakly); 'and' joining two adjectives or two verb phrases ('cold and wet', 'cooked dinner and cleaned the kitchen'); 'the' + one noun repeated ('the book ... the book'); words separated only by spaces; 'than' comparisons are mostly silent too (about one in four crosses).
